title: Beijing says US firms train AI models on Chinese examples
summary: Beijing accused US artificial intelligence companies of using Chinese examples to train and distill AI models, calling recent US accusations baseless and accusing Washington of "AI hegemonism." The statement follows US threats of sanctions tied to alleged theft of proprietary models and heightened scrutiny after Chinese startup Moonshot AI released a high-profile model, the Kimi K3.
content:
East Asia

"It is understood that many American artificial intelligence enterprises have distilled Chinese models during their research, development and training processes," says the Chinese commerce ministry.

People visit the Moonshot AI stand, featuring the Kimi K3 model, during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai on Jul 18, 2026. (File photo: AFP/Hector Retamal)

BEIJING: Beijing accused US artificial intelligence companies on Monday (Jul 27) of using Chinese examples to train their models, days after Washington threatened sanctions on Chinese firms for allegedly stealing American technology.

"It is understood that many American artificial intelligence enterprises have distilled Chinese models during their research, development and training processes," the Chinese commerce ministry said in a statement.

Distillation is a process in which an AI model is trained to mimic the output of a larger, more capable one.

The method is widely used across the industry, but US officials say Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy proprietary American systems.

The Chinese ministry said the US accusations "lack factual basis and legal grounds, adopt double standards in practice, and constitute typical acts of artificial intelligence hegemonism." "China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests," it added.

Last week, a senior White House official accused Chinese startup Moonshot AI of covertly copying Anthropic's most advanced model to build its Kimi K3. The latest Moonshot model stunned the US tech industry upon its release, setting off a fresh discussion over the AI rivalry with China.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week threatened sanctions against China, amid reports the US is also weighing a ban or curbs on foreign-made open-source models that are often built through distillation.

The exchange highlights mounting tensions between Washington and Beijing over technology, intellectual property and the global race to develop advanced AI systems. Beijing framed the US actions as politically motivated and warned it would protect Chinese companies and interests if measures were adopted against Chinese firms.

Analysts say the debate underscores the challenge of policing AI research practices that are widespread in the industry, including model distillation and reuse of training data, while balancing national security and commercial concerns.
